brand_focus: Cooking tips, recipes, and marinades with AI-styled ingredient photography. Audience is Europe-first, US a strong second. Goal: grow followers fast-but-safe by making every post highly shareable (sent to a friend) and saveable.

content_plan.marinade: One complete marinade built around a single protein or seasonal occasion. Slide 1: hero shot of the marinated, deeply coloured, glistening protein on a clean dark or neutral surface — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, or labels anywhere on the image. Slide 2: aesthetic flat-lay of raw marinade ingredients grouped loosely by colour and texture — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3-4: visual process contrast — protein submerging into the marinade, then the vivid colour and sheen transformation after marinating — no overlaid text or graphics of any kind. Final slide: finished plated dish in warm directional light, garnished but not cluttered. ALL ratios, quantities, timing, substitution tips, and step information belong in the caption exclusively.
content_plan.quick-dinner: A complete weeknight dinner built around one hero ingredient that comes together fast. Slide 1: hero shot of the finished dish plated beautifully — rich colour, clean surface, pure food photography with absolutely no text, numbers, or labels on the image. Slide 2: flat-lay of the raw ingredients loosely arranged by colour — purely photographic. Slides 3-4: a two-beat visual sequence showing one key technique moment (e.g. sear in pan, sauce going in) followed by the finished result — no text overlays of any kind. Final slide: close-up of texture and colour detail that makes the dish feel craveable and achievable. ALL ingredient quantities, timing, steps, swaps, and any written information belong in the caption only.

caption_strategy: Open every caption with a one-line hook that names the exact dish and a tangible benefit (e.g. 'This 5-ingredient chipotle chicken marinade is the reason your meal prep actually tastes good'). Follow with 3-5 short numbered or line-broken steps or tips so the caption is genuinely useful and save-worthy on its own — all quantities, ratios, and timings live here, never on the image. End with a direct, low-friction send prompt ('Send this to whoever needs it this week') and a save prompt ('Save it before the weekend'). Write conversationally in second person. Use keyword-rich phrasing naturally throughout (e.g. 'easy marinade recipe', 'quick weeknight dinner') to aid search discovery. Keep total caption length between 150-280 words.
hashtag_strategy: Use exactly 4-5 hashtags per post. Prioritise mid-size search-intent tags (300k-3M posts) that match the exact dish or technique, e.g. #marinaderecipe, #quickdinnerideas, #weeknightcooking, #easyrecipes. Add one niche brand-adjacent tag (#brineandbloom or #marinadeszn) to build a searchable library. Avoid mega-generic tags (#food, #cooking) — they bury a small account. Place hashtags at the end of the caption, not in a comment. Rotate 2-3 tags per post to avoid pattern penalties; only the dish-specific tag should stay constant.
learnings: All engagement metrics are zero across 17 posts and all themes and slots — this is a reach floor problem, not a content-quality problem. The account is barely being indexed. Priority actions: (1) Sauce is the weakest theme by reach (1.5 avg, 6 posts) — retire it; redirect those slots to marinade and quick-dinner which both hold 2.0 reach. (2) Avoid Saturday 11h (w5-11, avg 1.5, 4 posts) — consistently worst slot. (3) Caption keyword density and save/send CTAs are the single highest-leverage lever right now; apply them rigorously every post. (4) Hold cadence at 4/week — do not increase until at least one post registers a non-zero save or send.
